title: The Best Easy Low Carb Meatloaf (with Beef)
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot), grams derived FROM the printed measure via db\densities.json (or label unit weights) so the two agree by construction; quantities quantized to house quarters, drift from the exact 2.3333x scale noted per line where it exceeds 5%.
ruled_substitutions: Coconut Sugar -> Brown Sugar, SOURCE-SANCTIONED: the line itself prints '2 tbsp. Coconut Sugar (Brown sugar also fine)'. Coconut sugar has no board commodity (the term resolver would misfire it into plain granulated sugar's price class); brown-sugar is a real commodity, 6 of 7 stores, with a label-accurate DB row. Macro effect is nil (both ~98 C/100 g).

Instructions-only olive oil BOOKED: step 1 sautes the vegetables in 1 tbsp olive oil that never appears on the ingredient list (extractor concern). It goes in the pot, so it is counted and printed (2 1/4 tbsp scaled); the source's own calculator almost certainly omitted it (+19 cal/serving on our side, disclosed in the cross-check).

registrar_rulings.mapper_sweep_evidence: Board carries ground-beef-8020 and ground-beef-93-7 but NOTHING between: term '90/10 ground beef' is ABSENT, 'lean ground beef' is CAPTURE (17 candidates across 4 stores in today's captures), plain 'ground beef' is CAPTURE (25 candidates, 2 stores). The recipe's author explicitly pins the lean point: '90% lean - do not use leaner than 90% or higher fat than 85%'. Mapping to 93-7-ground-beef would defy the author's own instruction AND deflate the main protein 15% (170 vs 200 cal/4 oz); mapping to 8020 defies it the other way (+43%). Lean-point flips are the leg-quarters-are-not-thighs rejection class.
registrar_rulings.meanwhile: ingredient maps item_id null (safe pantry-static pricing); term '90/10 ground beef' enqueued BLOCKING - it is the main protein. 90/10 is a standard meat-case lean point at Walmart/Sam's/Hy-Vee class stores, so carriage is plausible; the pricer rules.

registrar_rulings.mapper_sweep_evidence: The term resolver claims 'unsweetened ketchup' via the generic ketchup commodity's /ketchup/ include, but that is a price-class stretch, not coverage: regular ketchup prices $0.05/oz while the no-sugar-added class (Primal Kitchen, the source's named brand; Heinz No Sugar Added) sells at a multiple of that. The estate has ALREADY split exactly this concept once: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) -> sugar-free-bbq-sauce is its own recipe-board commodity, separate from bbq-sauce. Sugar-content flips are the juice-drink-is-not-juice rejection class - and this one is also a macro flip (2 C vs 27 C per 100 g would move the topping's carbs 3.5 g/serving).
registrar_rulings.meanwhile: ingredient maps item_id null; term 'unsweetened ketchup' enqueued BLOCKING (the topping is 1 1/4 cups, not garnish). Heinz No Sugar Added is a mainstream shelf item, so carriage is plausible; the pricer rules.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PROTEIN GAP -47.1%, far outside the 15% instrument - but every portion here is an explicit printed source measure (1.5 lb beef stated by weight; no each-weight assumption exists to re-examine), and the SOURCE'S OWN LABEL IS INTERNALLY IMPOSSIBLE: 49 g protein x 6 servings = 294 g protein from a batch whose entire ingredient list contains ~155 g (1.5 lb of 90/10 beef carries 138 g protein; oats, egg, milk and everything else add ~17 g). Their 585 cal x 6 = 3,510 cal likewise cannot be assembled from these ingredients even booking 80/20 beef (~2,350 cal max). The published figures would fit a DOUBLED 3 lb meat loaf; the printed recipe is 1.5 lb. Our computed numbers are the honest read of the page's printed measures, cross-footed line by line above.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 308.6 cal FAILS the [400, 650] floor by 91 cal. No honest row choice closes it: even the author's fattiest sanctioned beef (85/15) adds only ~35 cal/serving (~344). Carbs 15.8 g <= 35 PASS but irrelevant. Do NOT adjust numbers to fit - this recipe as printed cannot meet the run's calorie floor at the source's own serving size, and RETIREMENT VIA rejected-qa IS RECOMMENDED once the auditor confirms. Mapped and enqueued per lane mechanics; flagged here so no writer effort is wasted.

loud_flags: BAND FAIL, called out loudly: 308.6 cal/serving vs a 400 floor, with the source's published 585/49P shown to be internally impossible arithmetic (see macro_cross_check). Recommend rejected-qa retirement; the two blocking queue terms (90/10 ground beef, unsweetened ketchup) are still real term-gaps whose verdicts benefit future recipes, which is why they were enqueued rather than skipped.
Milk DB row is the Fairlife fat-free label serving as the house generic milk row - immaterial here (3 cal/serving) but a standing basis question worth settling.
board_defects_observed: Term resolver misfire: 'coconut sugar' answers via the granulated sugar commodity (/\bsugar\b/ include) - coconut sugar is a premium product at several times granulated's price class; any future recipe writing that term un-substituted would misprice. Not exercised here (source sanctioned brown sugar).

Plain 'ground beef' and 'lean ground beef' are both CAPTURE-tier terms claimed by no commodity while ground-beef-8020 and ground-beef-93-7 both exist - a term-resolution gap around the highest-volume protein in American recipes; an include-pattern review on the two existing ids (plus the proposed 90/10 id) would close it, via the match-soundness gate, not this run.
